subject: Convex hulls: exact turns and outer boundaries
conventions: Cartesian x right/y up; orientation is (bx-ax)(cy-ay)-(by-ay)(cx-ax). Positive means a left turn. This explorer retains only extreme hull vertices, starts polygon output at the lexicographically smallest coordinate, and follows counterclockwise order. Empty, point and segment hulls are explicit. Duplicate input identities remain visible although computation uses unique coordinates.

questions.prompt: For a finite set of planar points, which object is its convex hull?
options: The smallest convex set containing every point
The shortest path visiting every point in input order
An axis-aligned box containing every point
Any polygon whose vertices include every input point

questions.prompt: For A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(1,2), what are the orientation determinant and turn of A→B→C?
options: −6, right turn
6, left turn
2, left turn
0, collinear

questions.prompt: For A=(−1,1), B=(2,1), C=(2,−2), what is the orientation determinant?
A lower chain ends with A=(0,0), B=(1,1), and the next sorted point is C=(2,2). Under the stated extreme-vertex policy, what happens to B?
options: It becomes an interior point of the plane
It is kept because its determinant is positive
It is copied twice to close the polygon
It is removed from the chain because the determinant is zero; it still lies on the final segment

questions.prompt: The input contains (0,0), (4,0), (4,3), (0,3), (2,1), and (2,0). How many extreme hull vertices are retained?
Another input occurrence of (4,0) is added to that same point set. Which statement is correct?
options: The hull gains a new geometric vertex
The geometric hull is unchanged; both input identities can still be recorded
The area doubles
The entire input must be rejected

questions.prompt: Sort (2,0), (0,3), (0,−1), (−1,2) by x first, then y for equal x. Which order results?
The lower chain is [(0,0),(1,2)] and next candidate is (2,0). The orientation determinant is −4. What is the next chain operation?
options: Finish with a triangle
Remove (0,0)
Keep both old points because −4 is nonzero
Remove (1,2), then reconsider the candidate against the shortened chain

questions.prompt: What is the canonical extreme-vertex hull of [(2,3),(2,−1),(2,1)]?
options: Segment [(2,−1),(2,3)]; (2,1) is an edge member
Point [(2,1)]
An error because equal x coordinates are forbidden

questions.prompt: For the points (0,0), (4,0), (1,3), which canonical hull ordering and area are correct?
What hull kinds result, respectively, from [], [(2,1)], and [(2,1),(2,1)]?
options: error, point, segment
empty, error, polygon
empty, point, point
point, point, point

questions.prompt: For n distinct points, why does sorting followed by two monotone-chain scans take O(n log n) time?
options: Every possible triple must be inspected
Each chain repeats a complete sort after every pop
The scans each compare every pair of points
Sorting costs O(n log n); each point is pushed once and popped at most once per chain
